items.name: OpenAI GPT-6 Sol & Luna
items.summary: OpenAI launched two cheaper GPT-6 models on Sept 22 — Sol ($2/$10 per million tokens) for coding and agentic work, and Luna ($0.10/$0.50) for high-volume routine tasks — cutting API prices about 50% versus GPT-5.6. They sit below flagship GPT-6 Astra and shipped the same day in the API, ChatGPT Work, and Codex.

items.name: Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5
items.summary: Anthropic's new flagship launched Sept 22 at $4/$20 per million tokens — 20% cheaper and 30%+ faster than Opus 5, with performance comparable to the pricier Fable 5.1 plus new containment safeguards that cut boundary-escape attempts ~85%. Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 are promised in the coming weeks.

items.name: China Telecom AI Xing4.0-29B-A4B
items.summary: China Telecom AI's open-weight (Apache 2.0) agentic MoE — 29B total params, 4B active per token — runs on a single consumer GPU and was trained end-to-end on Huawei Ascend 910C NPUs with zero Nvidia hardware in the loop. It plans multi-step tasks, calls tools, and is available now on Hugging Face and GitHub.

items.name: Xiaomi MiMo-V2.6
items.summary: Xiaomi open-sourced MiMo-V2.6 Pro (1.02T params, 42B active) and Flash under MIT license on Sept 21–22, with Pro topping the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index for open-weights models at 46 — level with Grok 4.7. Xiaomi also published the full RL training stack, 7,000+ task environments, and the live-streamed training run's costs (~$2.62M for Pro).

items.name: xAI Grok 4.7
items.summary: xAI's Sept 21 update ships a larger base model (~2.1T params) with a longer RL run aimed at multi-hour agentic tasks, at the same $2/$6 price and speed as Grok 4.6 — live in the Grok app, Cursor, Grok Build, and the API. Vendor benchmarks show Terminal-Bench 4.0 nearly doubling to 38.0%, though independent testers flag higher token burn.
